requirement:
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the execution-coverage
chapter of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index` for each recorded nextest
test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt, test-attempt outcome,
and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented first-party Rust
source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed from unexecuted
lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to the
execution-coverage chapter.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
rationale: I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.test-coverage.index.details`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request implementation source. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** - **A detail subchapter under the execution-coverage chapter for each recorded test process, identifying binary, test name, attempt, outcome and originating run.** - `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` records two tests in two runs. - It asserts that the index has five sub-items (attempts, captured sources and file notes). - It asserts that every "Test process coverage" detail page is linked from the index by a `chapter_href`-derived href. - Each page must contain `Binary: binary`, `Attempt: 1`, `Outcome: success` and a capture timestamp. - The detail page for test "one" must contain `Test: one` and `Run: {first_run}`, so the originating run is checked. - `fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` asserts that the pages sit under the coverage chapter. It checks `parent_names`, paths and section numbers with both numbered and unnumbered parents. - **Instrumented source lines and execution counts, with executed and unexecuted lines distinguished, using the source captured for that run.** - `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs` test "process reports preserve counters, source text, child identity and lazy file rendering" feeds the viewer a `u64::MAX` count and a zero count. It asserts the output contains `18446744073709551615 executed` and `0 unexecuted`. - The same test checks that source is rendered literally (``), that a message from an unrelated window is ignored, and that a message for the wrong run is ignored. - In the Rust test, the source file is overwritten after recording. The pages must still contain `fn one() {}` and the saved counts, so the captured source is what gets shown. - `fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` shows that the captured source remains on the detail pages when the live source has changed and the view is stale. - `fn[rendered_detail_scripts_remain_literal_across_blank_lines]` renders the detail page through `pulldown_cmark`. It asserts that the viewer script and the counter JSON survive intact. - **A link back to the execution-coverage chapter.** The Rust test asserts that every detail page contains `[Back to coverage index](../coverage.html)`. - **Child-process coverage distinguishable from the test process's own.** - The Rust test asserts that the page's data carries `"kind":"Test"` and `"kind":"Child"`, and that the child's counts appear (`"1":"0","2":"7"`). - The JS test asserts a separate "Child process 2" section and that the child's source stays out of the closed section until it is opened. **Residual observations (not gaps)** - Only `success` outcomes are asserted on the detail page. The outcome is displayed from the recorded attempt, and the failed and interrupted outcomes are exercised on the index in `fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]`. I did not treat this as a missing obligation. - The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so I found no marking gap.

text: :::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the execution-coverage
chapter of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index` for each recorded nextest
test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt, test-attempt outcome,
and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented first-party Rust
source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed from unexecuted
lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to the
execution-coverage chapter.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
:::{req} index
`habeas mdbook` MUST automatically generate exactly one execution-coverage
subchapter under the requirements index of
{cite}`requirements.index.chapter`, whether that requirements index is
explicitly placed or automatically generated.
